newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Land claim move boosts uncertainty - cattlemen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Land claim move boosts uncertainty - cattlemen.

text.p: The decision by Australia's High Court to allow Aboriginal land claims to co-exist with the rights of pastoralists meant increased uncertainty for pastoral leaseholders, cattlemen's lawyer Mark Love said on Monday.
Love, who represented the Cattlemen's Union in the case, said the ruling meant farmers would now have to look at exactly what rights they hold in regard to their land.
"Obviously, we're disappointed with the outcome of the case (because) it hasn't delivered the degree of certainty that we had hoped for," Love told reporters outside the court.

"Essentially what it means is that the court made it clear that native title yields in the face of the rights granted under ... a lease, but we've now got to go back and determine precisely what rights have been granted to the cattlemen." The High Court found that the claim of an Aboriginal group, the Wik people, over 35,000 square km of land in the state of Queensland may extinguish the rights of the 12 pastoral leaseholders in that area.

Love said it appeared the judgment was limited to the leases in the Cape York area of far-north Queensland, but it was too early to determine what implications the decision had for the rest of Australia.
"We would hope to be able to pull from the judgments some guidance as to how native title will pursue and how other land tenures can stand consistently with that," he said.
